evals.prompt: Create a new customer with custom ID 'my-app-user-42'
evals.expected_output: Code that POSTs to /service/customers with custom_id='my-app-user-42' and company-level auth headers
assertions: The code sends a POST request to /api/v3/service/customers
The request body includes 'custom_id' set to 'my-app-user-42'
The request includes 'company-id' and 'license-token' headers
The code extracts data.id as customer-id and data.access.token as access-token from the response

evals.expected_output: Code that GETs /service/customers with company-level auth headers
assertions: The code sends a GET request to /api/v3/service/customers
The request includes 'company-id' and 'license-token' headers
The code handles pagination parameters (limit/offset) or displays results

evals.prompt: Get the customer with custom ID 'user-abc'
evals.expected_output: Code that GETs /service/customers/custom-id/user-abc with company-level auth headers
assertions: The code sends a GET request to /api/v3/service/customers/custom-id/user-abc
The request includes 'company-id' and 'license-token' headers
The code parses the customer model from the response

evals.expected_output: Code that sends DELETE to /service/customers/cust-123 with company-level auth headers
assertions: The code sends a DELETE request to /api/v3/service/customers/cust-123
The request includes 'company-id' and 'license-token' headers
The code checks for 204 No Content response

evals.expected_output: Code that GETs /service/licenses with company-level auth headers
assertions: The code sends a GET request to /api/v3/service/licenses
The request includes 'company-id' and 'license-token' headers
The code displays license information from the response

evals.prompt: Set up a webhook on license lic-456 to receive notifications at https://my-server.com/mubert-webhook
evals.expected_output: Code that PUTs /service/licenses/lic-456 with webhook_url and webhook_enabled=true
assertions: The code sends a PUT request to /api/v3/service/licenses/lic-456
The request body includes 'webhook_url' set to 'https://my-server.com/mubert-webhook'
The request body includes 'webhook_enabled' set to true
The request includes 'company-id' and 'license-token' headers

evals.prompt: Write a TypeScript script that creates a customer and then generates a track using the returned credentials
evals.expected_output: TypeScript code that first POSTs to /service/customers, extracts data.id and data.access.token, then POSTs to /public/tracks using those credentials
assertions: The code is written in TypeScript
The code first creates a customer via POST /api/v3/service/customers
The code extracts customer-id and access-token from the create response
The code then uses those credentials to call POST /api/v3/public/tracks
The service call uses company-id + license-token headers
The track generation call uses customer-id + access-token headers

evals.prompt: I lost the access token for customer 'user-abc'. How do I get it back?
evals.expected_output: Look the customer up by custom ID (read-only) and read data.access.token; reposting the same custom_id also returns the identical token
assertions: The answer retrieves the existing token rather than claiming it is unrecoverable
It uses GET /api/v3/service/customers/custom-id/user-abc (or POST /service/customers with the same custom_id) with company-id + license-token headers
It reads the token from data.access.token
It does not invent a token-refresh or regenerate endpoint

evals.prompt: Show me the usage limits for the customer with custom ID 'user-abc'
evals.expected_output: Code that reads data.access.customer_limits from a customer response
assertions: The code reads the limits from data.access.customer_limits, nested inside access
The code does NOT read data.customer_limits (that key does not exist and raises KeyError)
The explanation notes that -1 means unlimited

evals.prompt: Write a Python webhook receiver for Mubert track-completion notifications
evals.expected_output: A handler that parses the request body as a JSON array of track objects and acts only on generations with status 'done'
assertions: The handler treats the payload as a list/array of track objects, iterating over it
The handler does not index the payload as a single object (no payload['id'] on the top-level body)
The handler does not expect a 'data' wrapper on the webhook body
The handler only uses the generation url when status == 'done'

evals.prompt: I need to set up Mubert for my app — create a customer and give me the credentials to generate music
evals.expected_output: Code that creates a customer via service API and clearly outputs the customer-id and access-token for use with generate/streaming skills
assertions: The code creates a customer via POST /api/v3/service/customers
The response parsing clearly identifies data.id as customer-id
The response parsing clearly identifies data.access.token as access-token
The output explains these credentials are used for track generation and streaming
